key_insight: A fault-tolerant bosonic sensing protocol preserves Heisenberg-limited time scaling under dephasing by storing the signal phase in an error-corrected qubit register.
engineering_relevance: The protocol could extend precision-sensing durations beyond the probe’s noise-limited timescale using controlled displacements, parity measurements, and resets.
method: Construct an optimal bosonic error-correcting code under a mean photon-number constraint.
Couple the probe to a repetition-encoded qubit register through controlled displacements.
Repeatedly measure boson parity and reset the probe to remove noise while preserving the stored logical phase.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical scaling: distance-d encoding suppresses logical failures to order p^((d+1)/2), with Fisher information scaling as NT² over sensing times of order γ_A^(-(d+1)/2).
watch_item: The guarantees require sufficiently small residual signals and a circuit-level bit-flip noise model; experimental robustness to broader hardware errors is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Fault-Tolerant Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Metrology with Bosonic Probes
